name: Strategic Play
description: Generic strategic-play arena: actors take moves in a shared state space under explicit rules. One move palette covers the three classic shapes — TERRITORY (claim and hold positions on a fixed map of fronts), COMMITMENT (simultaneous moves committed blind and revealed together, payoff-matrix style), and SEALED BIDS (hidden offers for a prize, revealed together). All moves resolve simultaneously each round: everyone commits against the same snapshot, nobody reacts to another's move within the round. Built entirely from kernel primitives — claimable slots (territory), a development deck (chance), sealed-bid auction resolution, and commit-then-reveal phase resolution.

phases.name: maneuver
phases.description: Every player commits one move against the same snapshot of the board; all moves are revealed and resolved together. Commit-then-reveal: no player sees another's move this round before choosing their own.

entity_types.name: Player
entity_types.description: A strategic actor competing in the shared state space — a rival firm, faction, bidder, or player.

properties.name: score
properties.description: Accumulated strategic gains — territory value, payoffs won, prizes taken. The victory metric.

properties.name: resources
properties.description: Commitment budget — spent on bids and stakes. Running dry means playing conservatively.

properties.name: territories
properties.description: Number of fronts currently claimed and held.

properties.name: boldness
properties.description: Willingness to escalate and press contested positions.

properties.name: foresight
properties.description: Planning skill — reading the board and timing claims and commitments.

properties.name: guile
properties.description: Deception and defense — bluffing commitments, holding ground under challenge.

properties.name: last_commitment
properties.description: The move this player committed last round (visible after the reveal).

actions.name: claim
actions.description: Stake a claim on an open front. REQUIRED parameter: `territory` — the id of the front to claim (see the board's open fronts: north_ridge, south_gate, east_market, west_pass, central_plaza, far_reaches). Succeeds only if your read of the board is right (foresight check) and the front is still open — a front holds one claimant. Claimed ground pays score and counts toward territories held.

parameters.name: territory
parameters.description: Id of the front to claim: north_ridge, south_gate, east_market, west_pass, central_plaza, or far_reaches.

effects_on_success.description: Claim the named front (one claimant per front; rewards fire on claim).

actions.name: contest
actions.description: Challenge another player directly — pressure their position, undercut their claim, force a confrontation. Opposed contest: your boldness against their guile. Winning takes ground in the standings; a failed challenge hands the defender the initiative.

effects_on_success.description: A won confrontation converts to standing, scaled by how decisively it was won.

effects_on_failure.description: A repelled challenge strengthens the defender.

actions.name: commit
actions.description: Commit a strategic move for this round — everyone commits blind and all moves are revealed together. REQUIRED parameter: `choice` — the move you commit to (e.g. 'cooperate', 'defect', 'escalate', 'hold_firm', or whatever moves the scenario defines). Optional `stake` — resources you put behind it. Your payoff depends on how your committed move plays against what everyone else committed.

parameters.name: choice
parameters.description: The move committed this round, from the scenario's move set.

effects_on_success.description: Payoff for a well-timed commitment, scaled by how well it was played.

effects_on_failure.description: A misplayed commitment is still revealed.

actions.name: sealed_bid
actions.description: Submit a hidden bid for the round's prize. REQUIRED parameter: `bid` — the amount you offer, from your resources. All bids are sealed: submitted blind, revealed together. Highest bid takes the prize and pays for it; everyone else keeps their money and gets nothing. Bid above your read of the prize's value and you win a loss.

effects_on_success.description: The prize, worth more the harder it was fought for.
The winner pays their clearing price.

actions.name: gambit
actions.description: Play for a development — draw from the deck of strategic developments. Cheap information-and-luck move: the drawn development applies to you immediately (windfalls, setbacks, openings). Use when the direct moves look unfavorable this round.

effects_on_success.description: Draw the next strategic development and apply it.

actions.name: hold
actions.description: Hold position — make no move this round. Consolidate, watch the reveal, keep your resources intact.

agent_archetypes.name: Expansionist
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Grabs ground early and everywhere — claims aggressively, contests anything contested, outbids on instinct. Vulnerable when overextended and low on resources.

agent_archetypes.name: Fortress Builder
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Takes few positions and holds them absolutely — claims only what can be defended, repels challenges, never overpays. Wins long games; loses land-grabs.

agent_archetypes.name: Opportunist
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Reads the other players, not the board — defects when cooperation is priced in, snipes fronts others fight over, bids only when the field looks timid.

agent_archetypes.name: Dealmaker
agent_archetypes.persona_hint: Plays the cooperative equilibrium as long as others do — commits to mutual-gain moves, punishes defection once, forgives after. Steady scorer, rarely spectacular.

slots.description: The high ground — hardest to take, commands the board.
The main approach — heavy traffic, contested early.
The revenue front — steady value, everyone wants it.
The flank — cheap to take, awkward to defend.
The center — symbolic and strategic, the prestige claim.
The frontier — overlooked, pays off late.

cards.text: Windfall — an unexpected backer arrives. Gain 15 resources.
Momentum — your last move lands better than expected. Gain 1 score.
Setback — a supply line fails. Lose 10 resources.
Intelligence — you learn how the field is leaning. Your next commitment is better informed (no immediate effect; play accordingly).
Opening — a rival's position weakens. Gain 0.5 score.

rules:
STRATEGIC PLAY — actors take moves in a shared state space under explicit rules.

HOW A ROUND WORKS: every player commits ONE move at the same time, blind — nobody sees another's move this round before choosing their own. All moves are then revealed and resolved together.

THE MOVES:
- claim(territory): stake a claim on an open front (north_ridge, south_gate, east_market, west_pass, central_plaza, far_reaches). One claimant per front; claimed ground pays score and counts as territory held.
- contest(target): challenge another player directly — your boldness against their guile. Win and gain standing; lose and hand them the initiative.
- commit(choice, stake): commit a strategic move from the scenario's move set (cooperate, defect, escalate, …). Payoffs land on the reveal.
- sealed_bid(bid): submit a hidden offer for the round's prize. Highest bid wins and pays; everyone else keeps their resources.
- gambit: draw a strategic development — cheap luck-and-information play.
- hold: no move; conserve resources and watch the reveal.

SCORING: 'score' is the victory metric — territory value, payoffs, prizes. 'resources' is your commitment budget; spend it on bids and stakes, and mind that it runs out. Play the scenario in the briefing: it defines what the fronts, moves, and prizes mean here.

termination_conditions.name: max_rounds
termination_conditions.description: Hard cap on the number of rounds (defensive only — scenario endings usually replace this).
